newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cargo plane missing after take-off.
newsitem.headline: Indian cargo plane missing after take-off.

text.p: A small Indian cargo plane, carrying two crew members and cargo, went missing soon after take-off from a Bombay airport early on Thursday, an official spokesman said.
"This is correct. After take-off it disappeared," Sadhu Singh, Deputy Director at Bombay's Air Traffic Control told Reuters.
The Fokker Friendship (F-27) aircraft was bound for the southern city of Bangalore.
Air traffic operators lost contact with the plane a few minutes after it took off at around 4 a.m. (2230 GMT Wednesday), other officials said.
Most Indian cities are experiencing monsoon rains and the Press of India news agency (PTI) quoted an airport official as saying "the weather was bad and raining with low patches of clouds."
Singh said the whereabouts of the aircraft was not known.
PTI said the navy and other agencies have been alerted to look out for the missing aircraft.
The aircraft's two-member crew was its pilot and co-pilot. It was owned by Elbee Cargo Services Ltd.
